items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: they went down with Bird, with Charlie Parker or somebody in there.

ctx.x: See now we’re getting in to [sounds like] Otto King’s world.
Yeah, we just loved Red. You know, I think they went down there with Max [Roach], they went down with Bird, with Charlie Parker or somebody in there. They called him “Albino Red.”

I wanted to ask you a couple of other questions. Is jazz education today, is it up to the task, or were there things that you were learning inside the big bands that are different or supersede or are better or are structured in a different way than jazz education today?

items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Lockjaw told me about a -- he tells me -- well, Lockjaw was hip to him... Lockjaw said one night... Bird came in... Jaws said, 'Buddy, he ran Bird crazy.'

ctx.x: Bostic must have been pretty young, too.

He was young, yeah, he was around my age. He was aroung -- yeah, he and I about the same age. But boy, he was a virtuoso on that horn, man, I mean -- and actually, what he made it big on wasn't really his style. He was in Bird vein, he played like Bird. But a lot of people didn't know that and you know, he just played like 'Flamingo'-type things and that's what they wanted to hear and that's where he made his gold.
